clinicalPearls: Results from an extra derivative chromosome 22 that carries additional material from chromosomes 11 and 22, producing effective partial trisomy of both regions
It almost always arises from a parent who carries the balanced recurrent constitutional t(11;22) translocation, through 3:1 meiotic malsegregation
Features include profound developmental delay and intellectual disability with marked hypotonia
Microcephaly, characteristic dysmorphism, ear anomalies with preauricular tags or pits, and micrognathia are typical
Cleft or high-arched palate and congenital heart defects are common structural anomalies
Genital anomalies, particularly in males, and renal abnormalities may be present
A carrier parent is usually clinically normal but faces a recurrence risk for future pregnancies, so parental karyotyping is essential
Diagnosis rests on karyotype supplemented by FISH or microarray to characterise the supernumerary derivative chromosome
reference.pathophysiology: Emanuel syndrome is caused by the presence of a supernumerary derivative chromosome 22 that contains a segment of the long arm of chromosome 11 together with proximal chromosome 22 material. This extra chromosome almost invariably originates in a phenotypically normal parent who carries the recurrent balanced translocation between chromosomes 11 and 22, whose breakpoints lie within palindromic AT-rich repeats that predispose to the rearrangement. During meiosis a 3:1 malsegregation transmits the derivative chromosome in addition to the normal pair, so the child has three copies of the involved 11q and 22q segments. The resulting over-dosage of the genes in these regions disrupts development broadly, producing the neurodevelopmental, craniofacial, cardiac, and genitourinary features of the syndrome.
additionalDifferentials: Other supernumerary marker chromosome syndromes such as cat-eye syndrome
Trisomy 13 or 18 presenting with multiple congenital anomalies
CHARGE and other malformation syndromes with ear and heart anomalies
Other chromosomal imbalances detected on microarray
Syndromic causes of profound developmental delay with dysmorphism
additionalInvestigations: Karyotype to identify the supernumerary derivative chromosome
FISH or chromosomal microarray to define the derivative chromosome content
Parental karyotyping to detect a balanced t(11;22) carrier
Renal ultrasound and genital examination for genitourinary anomalies
Hearing assessment and evaluation of feeding and airway
redFlags: Airway compromise related to micrognathia and hypotonia
Feeding failure with aspiration risk from cleft palate and hypotonia
Severe apnoea or respiratory instability in the newborn period
reference.prognosis: Most affected individuals survive infancy but have profound intellectual disability with limited communication and mobility, and lifelong care is required; life expectancy depends chiefly on the severity of associated cardiac, airway, and feeding problems, and complications of these often determine the long-term outcome.
pitfalls: Failing to karyotype both parents, thereby missing a balanced translocation carrier and underestimating recurrence risk
Relying on microarray alone, which may not fully reveal the structure of the supernumerary chromosome without karyotype and FISH
Overlooking associated cardiac or renal anomalies that need active management
Assuming a sporadic event when the recurrent t(11;22) origin is far more likely
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: No disease-specific therapy exists; management is supportive with early developmental intervention, physiotherapy and communication support for profound delay and marked hypotonia
Feeding support with attention to safe swallowing, and gastrostomy where oral feeding is unsafe
Surgical repair of cleft palate and correction of congenital heart defects
Airway assessment and management for micrognathia and associated airway anomalies
Surveillance and management of associated renal and genital anomalies
Hearing assessment and support, with treatment of recurrent ear problems
Multidisciplinary care coordinating paediatrics, clinical genetics, cardiology, surgery and therapy services
Genetic counselling with parental karyotyping for the balanced t(11;22) translocation and recurrence-risk advice
